flawed_step: No numbered proof is supplied. The first required substantive step—deducing Hamiltonicity from 3-regularity and 3-connectivity—cannot be justified, because the Petersen graph satisfies both hypotheses but has no Hamiltonian cycle.
counterexample: Take the Petersen graph with vertices a_i,b_i for i modulo 5 and edges a_i-a_{i+1}, a_i-b_i, and b_i-b_{i+2}. It is simple and every vertex has degree 3. To check 3-connectivity explicitly, identify its vertices with the 2-subsets of {1,2,3,4,5}, joining two vertices exactly when the subsets are disjoint, via a0=12,a1=34,a2=15,a3=23,a4=45,b0=35,b1=25,b2=24,b3=14,b4=13. Relabeling {1,...,5} reduces deletion of any two vertices to either the disjoint-pair case {12,34} or the intersecting-pair case {12,13}. After deleting 12 and 34, the remaining vertices lie on the spanning path 25-14-35-24-15-23-45-13. After deleting 12 and 13, they lie on the spanning path 45-23-14-35-24-15-34-25. Consecutive labels in each path are disjoint, so every deletion of two vertices leaves a connected graph. To check non-Hamiltonicity, suppose a Hamiltonian cycle existed. Since the graph is cubic, its unused edges would form a perfect matching M. Let k be the number of spokes a_i-b_i in M. The 5-k unmatched outer vertices must be paired by outer edges, so k is odd. If k=3, the two remaining indices would have to differ by 1 for their outer vertices to be matched and by 2 for their inner vertices to be matched, which is impossible. If k=5, deleting M leaves the separate outer and inner 5-cycles. If k=1, rotate indices so the selected spoke is a0-b0. The unique completion is M={a0-b0,a1-a2,a3-a4,b1-b3,b2-b4}; its complement consists of the two disjoint 5-cycles a0-a1-b1-b4-a4-a0 and a2-a3-b3-b0-b2-a2. Thus the complement of every perfect matching is disconnected and cannot be a Hamiltonian cycle.
assessment_summary: The explicit Petersen graph is finite, simple, 3-regular, remains connected after deletion of any two vertices, and is non-Hamiltonian. Therefore the universal statement is false.
